prompt:
A desktop web page for Lorenzo Germini's personal site, its /path page, rendered edge to edge at a wide desktop viewport with crisp readable text, no browser window, device or desk around it. The visitor watches his career play out as a tabletop board game that moves by itself, and can jump to any step.

The attached screenshot contributes only the page frame and the overlay regions: the top bar with "Lorenzo Germini" and "AI PRODUCT ENGINEER" at left, a "Flat site" link and a round dark-mode toggle at right, the step list at left, the text panel. Its grey 3D model is a placeholder: replace it entirely.

The hero, filling most of the viewport, is a 3D board seen from a high three-quarter view: a closed loop of seven large tiles with coloured bands, each carrying one small modelled landmark. Cuneo home is the start corner: the twin-peaked Bisalta behind a wedge plateau between two rivers. Then Turin (the Mole Antonelliana wrapped by two copper coils), Switzerland (a lake with the Jet d'Eau), Cuneo (a schoolroom with one dimmed window), Lille, Cuneo (a desk and an office), and ? (a blank card with five empty slots). Lille is selected and its scene stands built up, larger than the rest: the Chamber of Commerce belfry, the Vieille Bourse arcaded courtyard ringed by a pipe loop, and a clock-hand dial above a plaque reading "10,000 m³ a year — projected saving". The pawn is frozen mid-hop in an arc, about to land on the Lille tile.

The overlay sits in the board's world. Left: the step list "Cuneo home", "Turin 2017–20", "Switzerland 2020–22", "Cuneo 2022–23", "Lille 2023–24", "Cuneo 2024–now", "?", with the pawn marker beside Lille and small ticks beside the steps already seen; under it, transport controls (previous, pause, next) made as the game's own pieces, not media icons. Lower right: Lille's text panel, "Lille 2023–24", "AI Engineer · GSK", then "Built anomaly detection and time-series forecasting for manufacturing operations, and semantic NLP for fault detection and maintenance decisions."

The only text on the board is the tile names and the Lille plaque: no prices, money, figures or other numbers anywhere.

The world is a printed paper pop-up board: the tiles are flat printed card in two-ink risograph colours (terracotta and slate blue on cream stock, visible paper grain, slight misregistration), and each landmark is a die-cut card that folds up from its tile, showing white cut edges and scored creases; the pawn is a folded paper cone. Flat even daylight with crisp contact shadows under each fold, on the page's warm paper ground. The overlay is printed on the same card stock; the transport controls are die-cut tabs.
